text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- A currency board fixed exchange rate system could be introduced in Bulgaria in April at the earliest when inflation might slow down, former finance minister Stoyan Alexandrov told the state radio.
-- Bulgaria's Construction Ministry had struck 38 privatisation deals in 1996 worth some 515 million levs, Balkan news agency said. @
-- Bulgaria is expected to cut its trade representative offices abroad by 65 percent by the end of the year because of budget cuts, outgoing Trade minister Atanas Paparisov said.

-- Bulgaria's outgoing cabinet is expected to submit to parliament draft bills covering the introduction of a currency board system by January 10, outgoing Prime Minister Zhan Videnov told the national television.

-- The International Monetary Fund said Bulgarian commercial banks should have five billion levs minimum capital and four percent capital-to-risk assets ratio three months after the introduction of a currency board system in the country.

-- Zero growth of Bulgaria's gross domestic product assumed in the 1997 budget draft is unrealistic, a fall between two and four percent is more likely, said National Statistics Institute's director Zahari Karamfilov. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
